main_text.l: inquit vobiscum sum, omnibus diebus
usque ad consummationem sæculi.] Et
in Epistola ad Cyriacum, eadem eiusdem
constantiæ pariter & obedientiæ elucet,
[cum à ciuitate inquit fugarer,dicebam
intra meipsum: si quidem vult Regina
me exulem agere, agat in exilium: Do-
mini est terra & plenitudo eius: Et si vult
secare, secet, idem passus est Isaias[?]:
si vult in pelagus me mittere, Jona recor-
dabor; si vult in caminum inijcere, idem
passi sunt tres illi Pueri: si me foris vult
obijcere, obijciat; Danielis in lacum Le-
onibus obiecti reminiscar: si me lapida-
re vult, lapidet; socium habeo Stepha-
num Proto-Martyrem: & si caput tol-
lere vult, tollat; habeo socium Johan-
nem Baptistam: & si substantiam auferre,
auferat; nudus exiui ex utero matris
meæ, nudus etiam reuertar.] Vox her-
clę digna, & fideli subdito, & infracto
Præsule, neq; alia illi post reditu mens.
[Dicite mihi, inquit, quomodo perse-
quuti estis Lupos? quomodo pepuliftis
Patrono? frequenti scilicet oratione ad
Deũ, quomodo despexistis adulteros ?
continuis lachrymis ex desiderio viri.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "Ifaias" (printed with a long-s-like form, read as Isaias, marked [?]). Long s rendered as plain s throughout ("si", "secare", "substantiam"), where the printed form resembles f. The initial I of Iona and Iohannem is read as J per the consonant rule; the printed form is I. The opening fragment "inquit vobiscum sum" begins mid-paragraph. No indented paragraph breaks are visible, so the page is one paragraph.
